# ↪️ Pull Request

Closes https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/4856
Closes #4840

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4779 has broken parcelrc in a different way:
Even when specifying an empty transformers map in an extending config, all named pipelines get order to the front types`:*.{ts,tsx}, bundle-text:*, data-url:*, url:*, *.{js,mjs,jsm,jsx,es6,cjs,ts,tsx}, *.{json,json5} , ...`, causing a JS script tag with `url:index.`js to match the `url:*` pipeline….

So it looks like the reordering the transformers is the wrong approach and it should rather keep the order and prefer named pipelines when doing the lookup.

- Actually, this is still wrong (but because of the design of our config format):.
```jsonc
{
	// custom config
	"*.ts": ["@parcel/transformer-typescript-tsc"], 
	// extended config
	"types:*": ["@parcel/transformer-tsc-types"],
	"*.{js,ts}": ["@parcel/transformer-babel"],
	"url:*": ["@parcel/transformer-raw"]
}
```

1. ~When giving named pipelines precedence:~
`<script src="index.ts"></script>` requests `url:index.ts` and matches `url:*` (wrong)
`"types": "index.ts"` requests `types:index.ts` and matches `*.ts`  (correct)
`import "index.ts";` requests `index.ts` and matches `*.ts`  (correct)

2. ~Use first match (with or without pipeline)~
`<script src="index.ts"></script>` requests `url:index.ts` and matches `*.ts`  (correct)
`"types": "index.ts"` requests `types:index.ts` and match `*.ts` (wrong)
`import "index.ts";` requests `index.ts` and matches `*.ts`  (correct)

3. Use first match (pipeline needs to match exactly if specified) 👍 
~`<script src="index.ts"></script>` requests `url:index.ts` and matches `url:*` (wrong)~
`<script src="index.ts"></script>` requests `index.ts` and matches `*.ts` (correct)
`"types": "index.ts"` requests `types:index.ts` and match `types:*` (correct)
`import "index.ts";` requests `index.ts` and matches `*.ts`  (correct)


Somewhat related to that (at the moment neither approach 1,2 nor 3 is used)

```
true  === micromatch.isMatch('types:index.ts', '*.ts')		   ???
false === micromatch.isMatch('types:index.ts', '*.{ts}')
true  === micromatch.isMatch('types:index.ts', '*.{ts,tsx}')   ???
true  === micromatch.isMatch('index.ts',       '*.ts')
false === micromatch.isMatch('index.ts',       '*.{ts}')	   ???
true  === micromatch.isMatch('index.ts',       '*.{ts,tsx}')
```

- Should the `NAMED_PIPELINE_REGEX` test be done once and stored for every pipeline? Rather doing it again on every match?

## 💻 Examples

```json
{
	"extends": "@parcel/config-default",
	"transformers": {
		
	}
}
```

## 🚨 Test instructions

Parcelrc above with `<script src="index.js"></script>`

The new logic is:

1. Don't reorder pipelines when merging configs
2. When matching a pipeline to a request:
	 -  find the first pipeline that matches the request's pipeline prefix (either same prefix or both have no named pipeline) and matches the glob, throw otherwise
	- get a list of all pipelines that match (starting again from the top) without the request's pipeline to resolve any eventual `, "..."`
Please open a new issue with all your config files + parcelrc

> This could be better suited in a separate PR

1. Commenting about the same issue in multiple issues/PRs makes it hard to follow the discussion
2. Commenting on a PR about a issue is generally a bad idea, since the discussion becomes basically invisible once the PR gets merged

`Transformation.js` didn’t take into account that asset.value.pipeline can change over the course of the transformation, which is why Vue was broken. A consequence of that fix is also https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4842#discussion_r511660315

> `Transformation.js` didn’t take into account that asset.value.pipeline can change over the course of the transformation, **which is why Vue was broken**. A consequence of that fix is also [#4842 (comment)](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4842#discussion_r511660315)

I don't believe the Vue transformer changes the pipeline of an asset at any point, but rather generates code that imports other assets with different pipelines. On a side note, we might also consider redoing the transformer with query parameters, since [that's what Evan You himself suggests](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/3364#issuecomment-622086191).
The `pipeline`/`type` changes when going from the `foo.vue` asset to the `style:foo.vue` child asset to the `foo.css` child asset.


```css

}
```

Output:

```js
console.log({});
//# sourceMappingURL=parcel.28ec9ebc.js.map
```

I expected a URL to be logged.

I suspect it's trying to access it as a CSS module? Maybe?

This seems different to https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/4498, but it might be a dupe.
